analysis:
The supplied changes are test-only: ServingConstructionPolicyTests.swift (head, lines 1-75) and ServingPerformanceProfileTests.swift (+30 lines, head 180-208). No production source, security control, wire protocol, key custody, or prefix-cache storage change is visible in this batch.

The tests exercise EngineV2Factory.productionServingPolicy and EngineV2Bridge concurrency admission. Automatic paged width on M5 Pro/Max/Ultra widens to 8 for allowlisted models. Unqualified fallback is 4 under power/thermal posture (hasPostureGatedWidth). Explicit operator widths are not widened or gated. Benchmark construction stays at the caller-supplied width. Tests also assert the serving/benchmark mixedStepPrefillTokenCap and soloPrefillStripe are preserved, and that service-budget leases are released (budget.serviceBudget.count == 0).

The likely related threat is T-041 (prefix cache / TTFT oracle), since wider concurrency could marginally change timing behavior. This is availability/throughput policy, not an accepted-risk change. T-010 and T-029 are only loosely related (DoS/resource use). I cannot verify the production implementation of hasPostureGatedWidth, productionServingPolicy, or servingChipIdentity because they are not in this batch. Integration should check that the non-test source changes in the same PR keep (a) the 8-slot width gated by posture, (b) the explicit-width path unchanged, and (c) no change to SSD cache TTL, scope or key derivation. No finding is raised from the test evidence alone.
